name: Thesis Evidence Draft — Materials Science
description: Compiles the EVIDENCE backbone of a materials-science thesis: materials, methods, per-experiment result chapters, characterization data, nomenclature — with full claim-to-source traceability. Interpretation, contribution and discussion are generated as structured scaffolds with [AUTHOR] placeholders: the argument is the researcher's. Demonstrates grammar v2: hierarchy (parent_key), repetition (repeat_for), auto-numbering, symbol registry, equation/figure blocks.

sections.title: Table of Contents
sections.notes: block_type 'toc' — rendered by code from the section tree + ref registry. Zero tokens, always current.

sections.title: Nomenclature & Symbols
sections.notes: block_type 'nomenclature' — rendered by code from doc_symbols, which auto-assembles from every symbol-bearing fact in the index (σ_y = 355 MPa in a datasheet registers σ_y). The registry is also injected into every generation call: chapter 7 uses σ_y exactly as chapter 2 defined it. Gap: symbol used in prose but absent from registry → warning.

sections.title: Introduction & Research Questions
sections.notes: Research questions compiled from sources; the motivation/contribution narrative renders as an author_placeholder block: '[AUTHOR: why this matters — your argument]'. The engine scaffolds, the researcher argues.

sections.title: Background & Literature
sections.notes: Compiles ONLY from reference PDFs the user has placed in the project (each indexed paper: citation, stated findings as facts). Per-paper summaries are traceable; the comparative SYNTHESIS is an author_placeholder. The engine must never claim to have surveyed literature it was not given.

sections.title: Materials
sections.notes: Composition tables from material certs (indexed PDFs). Every wt% cites its cert.

sections.title: Results: {item}
sections.notes: GRAMMAR V2 CORE: instantiated once per item in artifact_model.experiments (outline pass proposes the list — 'found: tensile series A, fatigue series B, SEM fracture study — 3 chapters?' — user confirms/edits). Each instance maps only its own files/facts. Micrographs and plots become 'figure' blocks with auto-numbers; stress-strain values cite data CSVs, never read off plots (confidence cap 0.5 rule applies). Each chapter ends with an author_placeholder: '[AUTHOR: interpretation of these results]'.

sections.title: Setup & Parameters
sections.notes: Child section (parent_key) — repeats with its parent. Numbered 8.n.1 automatically.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.notes: The engine generates ONLY a factual bridge: 'Chapter {{ref}} showed X {{fact}}; chapter {{ref}} showed Y {{fact}}' — cross-referenced restatement of what the evidence chapters contain. The comparison's MEANING is an author_placeholder block. This is the hardest honesty boundary in the product; it is enforced by required_content, not by hope.

sections.title: Data & Source Register
sections.notes: Every dataset, micrograph, cert and paper in the index — with captions and citing chapters. For a thesis: the reproducibility appendix examiners ask for. Code, zero tokens.

sections.title: Declaration
sections.boilerplate: The evidence chapters of this draft were compiled from the project source material listed in the Data & Source Register; all factual claims are traceable to the cited sources. Sections marked [AUTHOR] and all interpretation, synthesis and argumentation are the author's own work. The compilation tool performed assembly and citation only.
sections.boilerplate_no: Evidenskapitlene i dette utkastet er sammenstilt fra kildematerialet i data- og kilderegisteret; alle faktapåstander er sporbare til de siterte kildene. Avsnitt merket [AUTHOR] samt all tolkning, syntese og argumentasjon er forfatterens eget arbeid. Verktøyet har kun utført sammenstilling og sitering.
sections.notes: The academic-integrity posture inside the document. This sentence is what makes the tool defensible in front of a supervisor or examination board.
